Inside the world’s deepest and longest subsea road tunnel —Niall Firth I’m currently around 1,000 feet beneath the North Sea, in a dark, dank cave. It smells weird. And I’m increasingly aware of the pressure from millions of tons of seawater just above my head. I’m under the iconic fjords of Norway to visit what will soon become the world’s longest and deepest subsea road tunnel—an exceptional engineering feat that will carry drivers deep beneath the North Sea. I’m here to understand how you make a 16.6-mile highway that sits 1,280 feet below the sea at its deepest point. And also—at a time when it can feel hard to get anything done—to reassure myself that ambitious engineering is still possible. That we can still make things.  Step inside Norway’s Rogfast tunnel and see how engineers are making it happen . This story is from the next edition of our magazine, which is all about engineering. But rather than rushing to build new power plants, companies could find part of the solution right under our noses—or, more precisely, in the transmission lines under our feet and above our heads. If data centers can limit the power they draw during high-demand stretches, they won’t need to wait for big infrastructure upgrades or build their own off-grid generation. The idea of flexibility isn’t entirely foreign to grid operators. But a new generation of software could make the process faster, smarter, and more precise for the AI era. title: Three things to watch amid Anthropic’s latest feud with the government
content: This story originally appeared in The Algorithm, our weekly newsletter on AI. To get stories like this in your inbox first, sign up here . For those of you enjoying your summer unaware of Anthropic’s latest feud with the US government, here’s a recap: In April the company said it had built an AI model called Mythos that was so good at working with code it could pose a global cybersecurity threat. Anthropic gave access to a small group of cybersecurity experts so they could see what they were up against. Then it released a modified version called Fable which it said was safer to the public on Tuesday, June 9. That Friday, the federal government told the company it was a threat to national security and placed export controls on the new release. Anthropic revoked access to both models hours later. People worried about catastrophic effects of AI—broadly labeled “doomers”—have said for years that the technology poses a threat to humanity and published proposals for how the government should intervene in its development. The doomers just got their government intervention—not over a bioweapon or rogue AI, but in response to an AI model that’s basically just really good at coding. And the result so far looks less like a safety plan than like a superficial reaction. There’s plenty to dissect about what happened in those few days that led to such drastic action from the government, and it’s notable that Amazon CEO Andy Jassy was the one who told government officials that Fable would be dangerous (Amazon is both invested in Anthropic and building its own competing AI models). It’s also possible this will be a short-lived ban from the government that doesn’t survive legal scrutiny (it’s not clear that Anthropic’s offering access to Fable really counts as “exporting” it, for example).  But there are ripple effects happening already.  For one, this is making a whole lot of people not want to rely on American AI companies. title: How Anthropic may have talked itself into an AI export ban
content: Anthropic has warned about the dangers of advanced AI far more often than rival OpenAI this year, according to FT analysis, as critics accuse the company of helping to trigger a US ban on foreign access to its newest models. Five in every 1,000 words used by Anthropic in 2026 related to risk, regulation, or restrictions, according to FT research that analyzed official statements, social media posts, and articles written by the company or its chief, Dario Amodei. The equivalent figure for OpenAI and Sam Altman was eight times lower, at 0.6 words per 1,000. The comparison has become politically charged after Washington last week barred foreign nationals from using Anthropic’s latest models, Mythos and Fable. content: サカナAIがマルチエージェントオーケストレーションのFuguをリリース。何なのかというと体験としては単なるLLMのAPI。料金プランはサブスクまたは従量課金。普通のFuguと高品質のFuguUltraの２種類。Fuguというのはサービスの名前でもあり、実際にSakanaAIが開発したLLMモデルの名前でもある。独自モデル作ったりしてる分OpenRouterのFusionとかより凝ってる。基盤になってる技術は「TRINITY」と「Conductor」という二つのサカナAIの論文。Fuguは上司AIとして内部的に他社の色んなモデルを呼び出して作業させてそれらを取りまとめてファイナルアンサーを出す。具体的に内部でどのモデル呼んでるか分からんけどまあGPT5.5とかOpusとか呼んで組み合わせてるんだろう。結果としてMythosやFableに迫るベンチスコアを叩き出しちゃってるのでAI遮断リスクに対してロバストだという。Fuguの狙いの素晴らしい点はFuguユーザはもうFableがいつ再公開されるんや～とかGPT5.5が遮断されたらどうしよう～みたいな個別的リスクに悩まされる必要が無いという点。サカナAIはFuguが内部的に呼び出すモデルのデッキ構築を勝手にやって性能を最適化し続けてくれる（に違いない）もしも今後GPT5.5とかが遮断されたらその時はFuguの呼び出しモデルが差し替えられる。多少性能が変わるかもしれんけど現状の最善性能を提供し続けてくれる（ハズだ）逆にFable再公開されたらFuguにも組み入れられてさらに性能上がるだろう。新しくGPT5.6とか出たらまた最適化していい感じに組み入れてくれるハズ。例えるならGPTとかOpusとかFableとかの個別のモデルが個別株だとしたらFuguはオルカンみたいなもん。個別株に全賭けしてる人はその会社の上昇下落でイチイチ一喜一憂するはめになるが、インデックスファンドなら組み入れ銘柄を勝手に最適化し続けてくれるので悩む必要ない。サカナAIはビジネスセンスあるのか心配だったけど現在の政府AI遮断の緊張感を逆手にとって金儲けに繋げてきてさすがに伊達じゃなく賢い

title: Rights groups demand release of Burkina Faso journalist held in secret detention
content: Burkina Faso’s authorities have failed to account for the whereabouts of journalist Atiana Serge Oulon two years after state security forces forcibly disappeared him, a coalition of rights groups said Monday, renewing demands for his immediate release. Oulon, who is the director of the newspaper L’Événement (The Event), known for his investigative reporting on governance and corruption, was reportedly taken by state security agents in June 2024 from his home in Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso’s capital. The joint statement was issued by Amnesty International, Human Rights Watch, Reporters Without Borders, Observatoire Kisal, and the Observatory for the Protection of Human Rights Defenders, a partnership of the International Federation for Human Rights (FIDH) and the World Organisation Against Torture. The groups warn that enforced disappearance is a crime under international law. They have urged Burkina Faso’s government to disclose Oulon’s location and condition, release him without delay, and investigate those responsible. Human Rights Watch (HRW) senior researcher, Ilaria Allegrozzi said : Several dozens of government critics have been unlawfully conscripted and deployed to combat zones without adequate training. This cruel practice appears intended to pressure critics into submission through fear and coercion. Reporters sans frontières (Reporters Without Borders, or RSF) reported in May 2026 that Oulon was held in private houses converted into detention sitesnear the US embassy in Ouagadougou, allegedly beaten, deprived of food, and denied access to lawyers or family members. Rights group including Amnesty , RSF , and Observatoire Kisal, have added their voices by jointly condemning his disappearance, calling it a deliberate attack on press freedom. Meanwhile, Burkina Faso is a party to the International Convention for the Protection of All Persons from Enforced Disappearance which classifies enforced disappearance as a crime under International Law,

title: When Trade Secret Claims Become Non-Competes by Another Name
content: On June 15, 2026, a federal court in San Francisco dismissed xAI's trade secret claims against OpenAI with prejudice. The dismissal came with prejudice for a reason that sits at the heart of this article: xAI had sought to keep the case alive long enough to obtain, in discovery, the evidence it lacked at filing. The court refused, holding that a plaintiff “was required to have completed its investigation of its claims before filing suit, not after.” Put differently: the court did not treat a job interview as a trade secret extraction ceremony. The post When Trade Secret Claims Become Non-Competes by Another Name appeared first on IPWatchdog.com | Patents & Intellectual Property Law .

content:
Claude Sonnet 5: separating the signal from the hype

Every few weeks the timeline lights up with "Sonnet 5 is coming next week." Slugs appearing on partner providers. A "Fennec" codename. 1M context, better vision, a new tokenizer. Here's the thing worth saying out loud: most of this is the same rumor cycle recycling itself, and you should hold it loosely.

What's actually verifiable:
• A `claude-sonnet-5@20260203` date string did surface in Google Vertex AI error logs back in February — that part is real and was widely reported.
• "Fennec" has circulated as an alleged internal codename across multiple outlets.
• Anthropic has never officially confirmed a Sonnet 5 launch, pricing, or benchmarks. Every "82.1% SWE-bench" number floating around traces back to blog posts, not Anthropic.

What's worth being skeptical about:
• "A slug appeared, leaks historically show up 5–7 days before release" is pattern-matching, not a source.
• The "30% more tokens on the same prompts" tokenizer claim has no traceable origin.
• Anthropic's *actual* current frontier is Opus 4.8 plus the new Mythos-class tier — not a shipped Sonnet 5. If Sonnet were the imminent headline, that's a strange gap.

Why the rumor persists: Sonnet is genuinely Anthropic's workhorse — the balanced, high-volume daily driver. A real upgrade there matters more to most developers than a flashy flagship. So the appetite is real even when the sourcing isn't.

My take: a next-gen Sonnet is plausible and probably inevitable. But "leaked next week" has been said since February. Treat slug-sightings as vibes, not roadmaps. When it ships, it'll be on https://t.co/AzsWX5qu53 — not a partner provider's error log. 🦊

Claude Code just crossed a line most people haven't noticed yet.

We're no longer talking about "AI agents."

We're talking about AI organizations.

Claude Code subagents can now nest 5 levels deep.

Not 1 agent calling a tool.

Not 1 agent spawning another.

A chain of specialists delegating work down the hierarchy.

Example:

main
 └─ project-auditor
     └─ structure-checker
         └─ import-validator
             └─ dependency-tracer
                 └─ style-sync

Each subagent gets:

• its own context window
• its own task scope
• its own reasoning process

And only the final summary bubbles back up.

Think about what that means.

The main Claude doesn't need to hold the entire project in memory anymore.

It delegates.

The auditor inspects architecture.

The checker validates structure.

The validator inspects imports.

The tracer maps dependencies.

The style agent enforces consistency.

Each one focuses on a single job.

Exactly like a real engineering team.

The crazy part?

Level 5 is a hard cap.

Meaning Claude can now create an entire chain of specialists before hitting the limit.

This changes how large codebases get analyzed.

Instead of:

"One giant context trying to understand everything"

You get:

"Many focused contexts understanding one thing extremely well."

The result:

• Better code audits
• Deeper investigations
• Less context pollution
• More parallel reasoning
• Cleaner outputs

We're quietly moving from:

AI assistants → AI departments.

And most developers still think Claude Code is just a coding chatbot.

They're about to find out it's becoming a management layer for teams of AI workers. 🤯

title: Windows 11 26H2 は 174KB の eKB で有効化。24H2/25H2 から即移行可能に
content: Microsoftは先日、Windows 11 の次期大型アップデートが 「26H2」 になることを正式に 発表 しました。すでにWindows Insider ProgramのExperimental/Betaチャネルでテストが始まっており、一般提供に向けた準備が進んでいます。 Microsoftは、「Windows 11 の次の年次アップデートはまもなく提供され、Insiderではすでに利用可能」と延べ、企業やIT管理者にとって「予測可能で低負荷なアップデート体験」を重視したリリースになると強調しています。 24H2/25H2からは「有効化パッケージ」で即アップグレード 今回の大きなポイントは、24H2と25H2から26H2へのアップグレードが 「有効化パッケージ(eKB)」 で提供されることです。 Microsoft が公開した新しい ホワイトペーパー によると、24H2、25H2、26H2の3つのバージョンは、同じサービスブランチ(Servicing Branch)を共有しており、基盤コードやテスト基準が共通化されています。そのため、26H2では、すでにデバイス内に存在している新機能をeKBによって「有効化」するだけでアップグレードが完了します。 有効化パッケージの特徴は次の通りです: サイズはわずか174 KB 再起動1回で完了 適用後のビルド番号は26300に更新 一方、23H2以前のバージョンはサービスブランチが異なるため、従来どおり6.5GBのフルアップデートが必要になります。 ハードウェア要件は？提供時期は？ Microsoftは、26H2でハードウェア要件に変更を加える予定はないとしています。つまり、24H2/25H2を動かしているデバイスであれば、そのまま26H2に移行できます。 現時点で26H2の正式リリース日は発表されていません。しかし、Windowsの「H2」アップデートは例年秋(9〜11月)に提供されており、今回も同様のスケジュールが予想されます。

title: Windows 11のLow Latency Profileを旧世代CPUで検証：8GB RAMでも体感改善
content: Windows 11に新しく追加された 「Low Latency Profile(低遅延プロファイル)」 は、スタートメニューや検索、アクションセンターといった各種シェル操作の反応速度を高めるための仕組みです。 操作した瞬間にCPUクロックを一気に最大値まで引き上げることで体感速度を改善する機能で、最新CPU向けの最適化と思われがちですが、実際は古いPCの方が恩恵が感じられるのかもしれません。 Windows Latest は、8GBのRAM、第6世代Core i3(i3‑6100)搭載の2016年製ミニPCでLow Latency Profileが効果的に機能していることを確認しています。 10年前のCore i3でも「反応速度」が明確に向上 テストに使われたのは、Lenovo ThinkCentre M700(Core i3‑6100／8GB RAM)です。Core i3‑6100はターボブースト非対応で、最大3.7GHzが上限という古いCPUですが、Low Latency Profileを有効化すると、以下のような変化が確認されました。 スタートメニュー ：表示が明らかに速くなり、押した瞬間に3.7GHzへジャンプ 検索 ：入力開始時のもたつきが減り、レスポンスが軽快に アクションセンター ：最も改善が分かりやすく、アニメーションの滑らかさが向上 このCPUでは、アイドル時の800MHzから最大クロックまでの立ち上がりが遅いことが体感の重さにつながっていました。Low Latency Profileはこのギャップを一気に埋めるため、古いPCほど恩恵が大きいという結果になっています。 有効化されていない場合は手動でオンにできる Low Latency Profileは2026年6月の月例更新プログラムに含まれていますが、機能は段階的に有効化されるため、全てのPCで有効になっているわけではありません。 Low Latency Profileが有効になっているかどうかを確認する明快な方法はありませんが、タスクマネージャーやHWiNFOでCPUクロックの変化を確認しながらスタートメニューの操作を行い、瞬間的に最大クロックへ跳ね上がっているかどうかで判定することはできます。 無効な場合は、ViVeToolを使って手動で有効化することもできます。 GitHub からViVeToolをダウンロードして展開。 管理者権限でコマンドプロンプトを起動し、ViVeToolのディレクトリに移動。 以下のコマンドで機能を有効化。 vivetool /enable /id:58989092 PCを再起動する 再起動後、上記の方法でCPUクロックが変化するか確認します。 古いWindows 11 PCでもまだ戦える 今回の検証では、10年前のデュアルコアCPUでもWindows 11の最新最適化がしっかり効くことが示されました。バッテリーや発熱への悪影響もなく、単純に反応が速くなるだけの改善です。 Microsoftは「Windows K2」プロジェクトのもと、WinUI 3によるシェル刷新も進めており、古いPCでもWindows 11の操作感は今後さらに良くなる可能性があります。

title: GM installs robots at flagship EV factory after laying off 1,300 workers
content: Dozens of new robot arms have been installed at General Motors’ flagship electric vehicle factory in Detroit—even as 1,300 workers remain out of work following what was supposed to be a temporary layoff. The latest automation push has spurred union pushback over a potentially existential issue for automakers and their workers. General Motors installed approximately 50 robot arms at GM’s Factory Zero plant in Detroit, Michigan, according to reporting by Crain’s Detroit Business . Made by the Japanese robotics company FANUC, the robots are designed to help attach various components to vehicles during the assembly line process. But leaders at United Auto Workers (UAW), the primary US union for autoworkers, reacted with anger to the new robotic presence, given how GM has not yet called back any of the workers affected by supposedly temporary layoffs in March. More than 1,000 union members are still “laid off indefinitely,” James Cotton, president of UAW Local 22, told The Detroit News . He said that the company could bring some of those members back to work instead of installing the 50 robots. Read full article Comments

title: The UK’s New Under-16 Social Media Ban Will Cause More Harm Than It Prevents
content: This week, politicians in the UK pushed forward with plans to eviscerate privacy and free speech on the internet by announcing a ban on social media for users under 16 that is set to take effect in Spring 2027. The UK government continues to falsely characterize this policy as a necessary response to growing concerns about online harms for young people. In reality, much like the Online Safety Act , it will cause more harm than it will prevent. Users of all ages are burdened with proving their age before accessing content, with social media platforms such as Snapchat, TikTok, YouTube, Instagram, Facebook, and X included in the ban. There remains no reliable, privacy-preserving method of verifying the age of every internet user and methods vary from one platform to the next. Young people will not simply be protected from being contacted by adults or endlessly scrolling—they’ll also lose access to educational videos on YouTube, local events on Facebook, and potentially cut off from distant friends and family. Public policy must be effective, proportionate and respectful of fundamental rights. Young people deserve better than a policy built on panic, and all internet users deserve a safe and free internet. A social media ban generates headlines, but it will not solve the problem. A Brief History of Age-Gating in the UK Age restriction proposals in the UK date back to a decade ago, when the proposed Digital Economy Bill was put forth to (among other things) restrict young people from accessing pornographic websites. While the Digital Economy Act of 2017 passed without age-based restrictions, it laid the groundwork for later age verification measures. Over the next few years, age checks for porn websites were announced then delayed several times . title: SquidのFTP コードに潜んでいた29 年物の脆弱性「Squidbleed」をClaude Mythosを即座に発見
content: Squidプロキシに29年前から潜んでいた重大な脆弱性「 Squidbleed (CVE‑2026‑47729)」が、AIによって発掘されました。 発見されたバグは、FTPディレクトリ解析の不具合が原因で、同じプロキシを利用する別ユーザーの平文HTTPリクエスト(認証情報やセッショントークンを含む)が漏えいする可能性があるというものです。 今回の発見で特に注目されるのは、脆弱性を見つけた研究者グループCalif.ioが、Anthropicの高度な非公開モデル Claude Mythos Preview を利用していた点です。 Mythos Previewは現在、一般には提供されておらず、AmazonやMicrosoftなど一部の大企業と、選ばれた研究パートナーだけがアクセスできる制限モデルです。Califはそのパートナー枠に含まれており、AIを使った深層コード解析プロジェクトProject GlasswingをAnthropicと共同で進めています。 今回の strchr の停止条件バグも、Mythosがほぼ即座に指摘したとされ、FFmpegなど他の巨大コードベースでも同様の「埋もれたパーサー系バグ」をAIが掘り起こしていることから、SquidのFTPコードは氷山の一角にすぎない可能性が示唆されています Squidbleedの正体：29年前の互換性コードが生んだ止まらない読み取り Squidbleedは、SquidがFTPディレクトリリストを解析する際の ヒープ領域の読み過ぎ(heap over-read) が原因で発生します。 Squidには1997年のNetWare互換性コードが現在まで残っており、 strchr() が ヌル終端(\\0)も検索対象に含める というC標準仕様の癖と組み合わさることで、ループが停止せずバッファ外まで読み進めてしまうというバグが発生することになります。 その結果、同じプロキシを利用する別ユーザーの平文HTTPリクエスト(Authorizationヘッダーなど)が、FTPのファイル名として攻撃者に漏えいする危険が生じます。HTTPSはCONNECTトンネルで暗号化されているため影響を受けませんが、平文HTTPやTLS終端構成ではリスクが残ります。 なぜ29年も見逃されたのか このバグは、以下のような条件が重なった結果、長年のコードレビューをすり抜けてきました。 古いCコード 歴史的互換性のための特殊処理 パーサーの複雑さ strchrの仕様という知っていれば気づくが、知らなければ絶対に気づかない罠 人間の盲点となる部分ですが、C標準仕様を丸ごと学習しているMythosは即座に異常を指摘したとのことです。AIによるコード解析が、古いOSSに眠るバグを掘り起こす時代に入ったことを示す事例と言えそうです。 [via The Hacker News ]
